Marta (sales): Hey team — Netriq's POC is failing when they try to run rerank after embeddings. Getting a dims mismatch error, customer says embeddings are 1536 but their reranker expects 768. They hit this in staging, blocking demo tomorrow.
Alex W: Ugh, classic. Do we know which model they used to produce embeddings?
Marta (sales): They used `text-embedding-3-large` per our quickstart. Example client call attached (they're using our hosted endpoint).
Priya R: Can you paste the exact error/log?
Marta (sales): Copying log from their engineer:
```
ERROR: RerankService: embedding dimension mismatch: expected=768 got=1536
  endpoint=/v1/re-rank
  request_id=cb4ef2
```
Sam G: That confirms it. `text-embedding-3-large` -> 1536 dims. Their reranker pipeline was built against an older 768-dim model. Two quick options: 1) change the embedding model to a 768-dim variant (`text-embedding-3-small`) or 2) update their reranker to accept 1536 (preferred long-term).
Marta (sales): Customer asked about "how much effort" to swap models vs change reranker. They want a quick workaround for the demo.
Alex W: Quickest is to switch to `text-embedding-3-small` in the client. Should be one-line change. If they need parity to large, quality will differ.
Priya R: I've pinged Netriq's engineer asking which SDK/version. @Sam G can you confirm any batching/size limits that might cause additional errors if they switch?
Sam G: Current hosted constraints: max batch size = 64 embeddings per request, payload limit = 2MB, rate limit per API key = 120 req/min (burstable). Switching to small will lower token usage, so should be fine.
Infra Eng: Also checking logs on our side for their request_id cb4ef2 — saw a 400 on the rerank call which matches the dim mismatch. No other infra errors.
Oncall Bot: Deploy completed to hosted-api:prod at 2026-11-03T09:17:12Z (sha: d4f3a2) :white_check_mark:
Marta (sales): Netriq asked about pricing impact if they run smaller embeddings for rerank at scale. Any quick numbers?
Priya R: For hosted per-embedding pricing: large= $0.012 / 1k embeddings, small = $0.006 / 1k (example tier). So switching saves cost but may affect rerank quality. We can run A/B on a small subset.
Alex W: If they want to keep 1536 dims for quality, we can offer two engineering paths: 1) we can help them add a thin PCA down-projector in their pipeline to convert 1536->768 (fast, introduces distortion), or 2) update their reranker model to accept 1536 (more work). I'm happy to jump on a quick call to sketch the PCA step.
Marta (sales): They accepted the PCA suggestion as a short-term patch. Can we provide a snippet they can drop in?
Alex W: Sure — small Python snippet using scikit-learn incremental PCA (fast-ish):
```
from sklearn.decomposition import IncrementalPCA
pca = IncrementalPCA(n_components=768, batch_size=256)
# fit on a sample corpus of netriq embeddings saved as numpy array
pca.partial_fit(sample_embeddings)
reduced = pca.transform(new_embeddings)
```
Marta (sales): Nice. Netriq also mentioned seeing intermittent 429s during encode when they did large batches in staging. They said it failed ~1/50 requests.
Sam G: That aligns with burst limits — if they push concurrent batches beyond 120 req/min we'll 429. Recommend they use `max_batch_size=32` client-side and add exponential backoff with jitter. Also we can temporarily raise the quota for the POC key if needed.
Priya R: I'll draft a one-paragraph note on recommended client settings and QOS for the POC and include pricing note + PCA snippet.
Infra Eng: If they want a quota bump for the demo, send the API key and requested rate and we'll patch for 24-48h.
Marta (sales): Perfect. I'll send them the PCA snippet + client config and offer a short troubleshooting slot with Alex for tomorrow at 10am PT. Also will tell them we can bump quota if their demo needs it.
Alex W: I'm available. If they want we can also run a quick Eval to compare small vs large embedding rerank quality on a 100-sample set.
Priya R: Added to follow-up: security questionnaire note — Netriq's legal asked about data retention. Reminder: hosted embeddings are stored for 30 days by default, can be disabled on enterprise plans. I'll loop in security if they need a custom retention SLA.
Marta (sales): Awesome, thanks all. I'll update the customer and post the outcome here after the call. :thumbsup:
Alex W: Thanks — ping me the dataset if they want the eval run.
Sam G: Marking this thread for follow-up; will watch for any quota bump requests.
